title: Wine Education & Teaching Methods
description: Designing and delivering effective wine education: adult learning theory, tasting-event hosting, certification prep, online formats, corporate training, and personal brand building

lessons.0.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 1 - 16 min
lessons.0.slides.1.title: The Special Nature of Adult Learning
lessons.0.slides.1.content: Wine education primarily addresses adult learners, who have clear learning objectives, rich life experience, and limited time. Effective wine teaching requires: (1) a practice-oriented rather than purely theoretical approach; (2) connection to learners' existing experience; (3) immediately applicable knowledge; (4) interaction and participation; (5) respect for different learning styles.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 📚 Instructional Design Principles
lessons.0.slides.2.points.0: Clear learning objectives — students should know what they are learning each session
lessons.0.slides.2.points.1: Theory meets practice — taste to verify immediately after theory is explained
lessons.0.slides.2.points.2: Progressive scaffolding — logical structure from basics to advanced
lessons.0.slides.2.points.3: Multi-sensory experience — visual, olfactory, taste, and tactile
lessons.0.slides.2.points.4: Repetition and reinforcement — key concepts revisited multiple times
lessons.0.slides.2.points.5: Assessment and feedback — prompt testing of learning outcomes
lessons.0.slides.2.points.6: Storytelling pedagogy — packaging knowledge in stories
lessons.0.slides.3.title: Level Design for Burgundy Courses
lessons.0.slides.3.content: Introductory (2–4 hours): geographical overview, basic classification, main varieties, 6–8 wines tasted. Intermediate (6–8 hours): deeper regional coverage, village characteristics, quality differences, 12–15 wines tasted. Advanced (12–16 hours): terroir analysis, iconic domaines, vintage variation, blind-tasting training, 20–25 wines tasted. Masterclass (thematic): single topic in depth (e.g., Côte de Nuits Grand Cru comparison, DRC vertical tasting).

lessons.1.slides.1.title: 🍷 Tasting Event Types and Design
lessons.1.slides.1.points.0: Introductory appreciation — 6–8 wines spanning different regional styles
lessons.1.slides.1.points.1: Vertical tasting — the same wine across different vintages (5–10 years)
lessons.1.slides.1.points.2: Horizontal tasting — the same vintage across different producers/parcels
lessons.1.slides.1.points.4: Themed tasting — e.g., 'Pinot Noir: A World Tour'
lessons.1.slides.1.points.5: Wine-pairing dinner — multiple courses paired with multiple wines
lessons.1.slides.1.points.6: Masterclass — in-depth thematic session (e.g., DRC or Leroy dedicated evening)
lessons.1.slides.2.title: The Host's Role and Techniques
lessons.1.slides.2.content: A great tasting-event host needs: (1) deep expertise without showing off; (2) facilitating rather than dominating discussion; (3) encouraging participants to express themselves; (4) handling differences of opinion with grace; (5) managing time and pace; (6) storytelling ability; (7) a sense of humour and warmth. Remember: your goal is to ensure participants gain knowledge and enjoyment — not to demonstrate how much you know.

lessons.3.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 4 - 14 min
lessons.3.slides.1.title: Challenges and Opportunities of Online Teaching
lessons.3.slides.1.content: Online wine education developed rapidly after COVID-19. Challenges include: inability to taste the same wine together, lack of in-person interaction, technical barriers. But there are advantages too: overcoming geographical constraints, ability to rewatch content, lower costs. Successful online courses require: pre-shipped wine samples, high-quality video, interactive platforms, and a post-class support community.

lessons.5.slides.0.title: Building Your Personal Teaching Brand
lessons.5.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 6 - 18 min
lessons.5.slides.1.title: Personal Branding for Wine Educators
lessons.5.slides.1.content: In a competitive wine-education market, personal brand is everything. The hallmarks of a successful educator: (1) professional certification as endorsement; (2) a distinctive teaching style; (3) a clear niche (e.g., focusing on Burgundy, or on beginners); (4) consistent content production (articles, videos, social media); (5) accumulated student recommendations; (6) an industry network.

lessons.5.slides.2.points.0: Clear positioning — your specialisation and differentiator
lessons.5.slides.2.points.4: Network collaboration — partner with importers, restaurants, domaines
lessons.5.slides.2.points.5: Professional image — website, business cards, teaching materials design
lessons.5.slides.2.points.6: Pricing strategy — reflect value without losing touch with the market
